discussion_comments.comment_body: Remote choice here is `branch.<b>.remote || origin`. `selectPrimaryGitRemoteUrl` in the workspace manifest uses `origin`, then the first remote. Two rules mean the manifest can show a different repo than the one this pushes to. Please unify them.

The selection rules remain different: handoff uses the current branch's remote, falling back to `origin`; manifest discovery has its own primary-remote preference. I have not marked this as unified. The confirmation displays the handoff plan's repository and remote, and both publication and cloud creation use that same plan, so the manifest cannot silently redirect this launch. Keeping the current selection in this PR avoids changing which repository existing branch configuration targets.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
Fixed in c739776f. Agreed on the root cause: `resolveAccountApiBaseUrl` prefers the provider `baseUrl`, while the link used `getClineEnvironmentConfig().appBaseUrl`, so a staging override with `CLINE_ENVIRONMENT` unset opened production.

`@cline/shared` now exports `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`, which maps the resolved backend to the environment that declares it (trailing slash ignored). The CLI resolves the account backend once, passes that exact base URL to `createClineAccountService`, and builds the link from `resolveClineAppBaseUrl(apiBaseUrl)`. A backend no environment declares (proxy, self-hosted) resolves to `undefined`, and `getClinePrivacySettingsUrl` now hides the link in that case instead of opening a different environment.

The same mismatch existed in the desktop sidecar `get_cline_app_base_url`, so it uses the same helper now. Tests: `resolveClineAppBaseUrl` (shared), `loadClineAccountSnapshot` links to `staging-app.cline.bot` for a staging override and hides the link for an unmatched backend, and the sidecar command returns `https://staging-app.cline.bot` / `undefined` likewise.

Please resolve the desktop app URL once at startup from the existing environment configuration and expose it as desktop configuration. We don't support switching the account/backend or environment after startup, so this doesn't need to run on each account refresh. Any startup provider override should be handled in that same configuration resolution. The webview still needs the resolved app URL passed across from the sidecar, but it doesn't need a separate account-driven refresh lifecycle.

the sidecar resolves it once at startup in [`728da6af`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/commits/728da6afab). [`index.ts`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-de4516568662afaa257a93b87322919abf6f8373f618c12105b06ba1f7543271R74) sets `ctx.clineAppBaseUrl` right after `createSidecarContext`, from [`resolveSidecarClineAppBaseUrl()`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-a9c19745939a47e95eaec39bdd97cf7f0bb114576e7d9d389d9a3a527fc6eb88R668) in `context.ts`, which reads the provider `baseUrl` override in that same resolution. `get_cline_app_base_url` [just returns the field](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-bc6a66091bf2af602bcea86b8eafccd68a2cc5a9c52d1c2432207cdcb5e798a2R3226) instead of reading provider settings on every call, and environment-scoped contexts inherit the value. covered by [`returns the app URL resolved at startup, for every environment context`](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15043/changes#diff-3d4567b52dd7fd16627866a2413bc613f7804f496eab4cfa1be309ffb11ad7d9R252).

I fixed this in 54ee82110. Clearing a custom base URL now sends an explicit `baseUrl: null` reset through the live connection contract. Core rebuilds provider configuration after removing the stale custom URL, so LM Studio returns to its manifest default while an empty string remains a distinct literal value. Regression coverage exercises the custom-to-default transition and transport parsing.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fair enough that `main`'s literal was already wrong for non-Cline providers; fixed properly in eb825d785. The connector now uses the provider manifest's `defaultModelId` when it is a real model (DeepSeek gets `deepseek-v4-flash`), skips the `"default"` placeholder exposed by catalog-less local providers, and only then falls back to `CLINE_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID`. Covered by a new case in `session-runtime.test.ts` for both the real-default and placeholder paths.

Keeping 15s as a single default, on purpose. Telemetry from the timed-out desktop devices: where the daemon did start, ~95% had it running within 7s of the old 8s cutoff, so inside 15s of launch. The 15-25s tail is a few percent of an already small group, and those devices still recover on the next launch exactly as they do today. 25s would also push the desktop worst case (up to 7.5s of login-shell PATH resolution + the wait) past the Tauri shell's 30s endpoint request. The cold-start cause is shared by every client that spawns the Hub from a compiled binary, so a desktop-only value would leave the CLI on the old limit for the same reason.
